We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}{5}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{1}{5}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}]}_{a}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[{5}^{x}]}_{a}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(5-{5}^{a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot (5-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y={5}^{x}$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{5}^{x}=0$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{5}^{x}=\infty $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14042659/assets/83f7d663fa66184b56c4f79d61f6e17012714a3de7512202b3022e91d4325437.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}{5}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot (5-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot (5-0) \\  & =\frac{5}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}.\end{aligned}
$$
